gloss: to make eye contact; eyes meet

definitions.gloss: to make eye contact; for eyes to meet
definitions.explanation: For two people to look at each other at the same time, resulting in mutual eye contact. Often implies a brief, sometimes significant moment.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}と{目|め}が{合|あ}った。
{電車|でんしゃ}の{中|なか}で{知|し}らない{人|ひと}と{目|め}が{合|あ}って、{気|き}まずかった。
examples.english: I accidentally made eye contact with a stranger on the train, and it was awkward.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}と{目|め}が{合|あ}うと、しっぽを{振|ふ}って{駆|か}け{寄|よ}ってきた。
examples.english: When I made eye contact with the dog, it wagged its tail and ran over to me.

notes: An intransitive expression — the subject does not actively choose to make eye contact; rather, it happens mutually. The particle と marks the other person: ～と{目|め}が{合|あ}う. Often used in romantic contexts to describe a meaningful first glance, or in everyday situations to describe accidental eye contact. Related expressions include {目|め}を{合|あ}わせる (to deliberately look someone in the eye) and {目|め}をそらす (to look away).
